questions.question: How do you debug Ruby with byebug and pry?
questions.title: Debugging with byebug and pry
questions.direct_answer: byebug is a step debugger: drop `byebug` in your code and execution pauses there — you can step (next/step), inspect variables (type a name), continue (c), and see where you are (whereami). pry is a powerful REPL and exploration tool: `binding.pry` pauses and drops you into an interactive shell where you can inspect, try code, and view source (show-source). pry-byebug combines both (pry's REPL + byebug's stepping). In Rails, `binding.pry` (or `byebug`) in a controller/model pauses the request; rails console --sandbox lets you experiment without saving. Remove breakpoints before committing. Use byebug to step through logic, pry to explore objects and try ideas interactively.

sections.title: Debugging Tools
sections.content:
byebug/binding.pry pause execution. byebug steps; pry explores (REPL, show-source). pry-byebug combines.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[code: byebug / binding.pry] --> P[pause execution]
  P --> B[byebug: next/step/continue]
  P --> Pr[pry: inspect, try code, show-source]
```

sections.title: byebug and pry
sections.content:
```ruby
# byebug: a step debugger
require 'byebug'

def total(items)
  sum = 0
  items.each do |i|
    byebug          # <- execution pauses HERE
    sum += i
  end
  sum
end
# At the pause: `next` (step over), `step` (step into),
#              `sum` (inspect), `c` (continue), `whereami`

# pry: a powerful REPL
require 'pry'

def tricky(obj)
  binding.pry       # <- interactive shell: inspect obj, try code
  obj.transform { |x| x * 2 }
end
# At the prompt: type `obj`, `obj.methods`, `show-source obj.transform`

# pry-byebug (gem): pry's REPL + byebug's stepping in one.
# Remove breakpoints before committing (they pause production!).

# Rails: rails console --sandbox  (experiment; rollback on exit)
#         rails console            (load the app; try models live)
```
